gloss: waitress at a traditional Japanese inn or restaurant

definitions.gloss: waitress at a traditional Japanese inn or restaurant
definitions.explanation: A woman who serves food and attends to guests at a ryokan (traditional inn) or traditional Japanese-style restaurant. The role involves not just serving meals but also providing hospitality and attending to guests' comfort.

examples.japanese: {仲居|なかい}さんが{料理|りょうり}を{運|はこ}んできた。
{旅館|りょかん}の{仲居|なかい}さんが{部屋|へや}まで{案内|あんない}してくれた。
examples.english: The inn's waitress showed us to our room.

examples.japanese: {仲居|なかい}さんが{着物|きもの}を{着|き}て、{笑顔|えがお}で{出迎|でむか}えてくれたのが{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: It was memorable how the waitress, dressed in a kimono, greeted us with a smile.

notes:
The polite form of {仲居|なかい}, always used with さん in everyday speech. Refers specifically to female attendants at traditional Japanese inns ({旅館|りょかん}) and high-end Japanese restaurants ({料亭|りょうてい}). The role goes beyond food service — {仲居|なかい}さん welcome guests, serve meals course by course, lay out futons, and ensure overall comfort. They traditionally wear kimono.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旅館|りょかん}の{仲居|なかい}さん: ryokan waitress
- {仲居|なかい}さんとして{働|はたら}く: to work as a nakai-san
- {仲居|なかい}さんが{布団|ふとん}を{敷|し}く: the waitress lays out the futons

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {仲居|なかい}さん is an iconic figure of Japanese hospitality culture. At a {旅館|りょかん}, the {仲居|なかい}さん assigned to your room is often your primary point of contact throughout your stay.
